advisories.title: Integer truncation in Valkey cluster publish message construction causes a heap buffer overflow
advisories.summary:
## Impact

An authenticated user who can publish to a channel on a server running in
cluster mode can make the server allocate a heap buffer far smaller than
the message it is about to copy into it, and then write past the end of
that buffer with attacker-controlled bytes. This reliably crashes the
server process, and because the overflowing bytes are chosen by the
attacker, it may be possible to escalate it to remote code execution
running as the user the server runs as.

This issue affects Valkey 7.2, 8.0, 8.1, 9.0, 9.1 and 9.2 running in
cluster mode. Servers that do not have cluster mode enabled are not
affected.

## Details

When a node propagates a `PUBLISH` or `SPUBLISH` to the rest of the
cluster, `clusterCreatePublishMsgBlock` in `src/cluster_legacy.c`
(`src/cluster.c` on 7.2) computes the length of the cluster bus message as
a `size_t`, but passes it to `createClusterMsgSendBlock`, which takes a
`uint32_t`. When the channel and message together exceed `UINT32_MAX`, the
length is silently truncated and a buffer far smaller than the message is
allocated. The two `memcpy` calls that follow copy the full channel and
message into it. Both the regular and the light cluster bus header paths
are affected, as are the module publish APIs.

Building a channel and message this large requires more than 4 GiB of
memory. With the default `proto-max-bulk-len` of 512 MB, a client cannot
send arguments that large directly, but a script can construct them on the
server.

The cluster bus cannot represent a message of this size, so the fix
validates the complete serialized length before any 32-bit conversion or
allocation. `PUBLISH` and `SPUBLISH` now reply with an error, and the
message is neither published locally nor propagated.

## Mitigation

You can mitigate this issue by using Valkey ACLs to restrict the scripting
commands (`EVAL`, `EVALSHA`, `EVAL_RO`, `EVALSHA_RO`, `FCALL`, `FCALL_RO`
and `FUNCTION`) if your application does not intend to use them, and by
not raising `proto-max-bulk-len` above its default.

## Credits

The defect was reported by Nenad Stojanovski working with Trend Micro Zero
Day Initiative (ZDI-CAN-28318). The fix was authored by
https://github.com/roshkhatri (#5030).

advisories.title: Unauthenticated use-after-free of the Lua interpreter state in Valkey (script debugger command cache)
advisories.summary:
## Impact

An attacker who can run scripting commands can free the Lua interpreter
state out from under the script debugger's cached command table, leaving a
dangling pointer that is dereferenced on the next debugger command. This
yields a reliable crash of the server process, and can be escalated to
control of an indirect call by reclaiming the freed heap chunk with
attacker-controlled bytes.

This issue affects the 9.x line. The defect was introduced when the Lua
scripting engine was moved into a Valkey module. The 8.0.x and 8.1.x lines
use the previous non-module debugger and are not affected.

## Details

`ldbGenerateDebuggerCommandsArray` in `src/modules/lua/debug_lua.c` builds
the interactive debugger command table once and caches it in a file-scope
static, binding the then-current `lua_State` pointer into each command
descriptor's context field. The table is never rebuilt or invalidated.

`SCRIPT FLUSH ASYNC` recreates the scripting engine, creating the
replacement interpreter state before freeing the previous one on the
lazyfree thread. Nothing clears the cached command table, so its context
is left pointing at a freed chunk. Any subsequent debugger command
dereferences it.

Because the freed chunk lives on the ordinary allocator heap, it can be
reclaimed with attacker-controlled bytes and shaped into a counterfeit
interpreter state, at which point the next allocation performed by the
interpreter calls the allocator function pointer stored inside that state.

A second use-after-free in `ldbLogStackValue` is fixed in the same change:
the logged module string was freed while the debugger log list still held
a reference to it.

## Mitigation

You can mitigate this issue by using Valkey ACLs to restrict the SCRIPT
command, in particular `SCRIPT DEBUG`, if your application doesn't intend
to use the script debugger.

## Credits

The defect was independently reported by Trung Nguyen (@everping) of
CyStack, by Phuc Nguyen Dinh (pucagit) of CyStack, and Han Sang-Kyung (toky1219@gmail.com).

The fix was authored by https://github.com/Baraa-Hasheesh.

advisories.title: Use-after-free in the RDMA pending-data handler when a client
advisories.summary:
## Impact

An authenticated user can run a command that frees another client's
connection while the RDMA transport is processing pending data, leaving a
dangling pointer that is dereferenced shortly after. This reliably crashes
the server process, and the freed heap chunk can be reclaimed with
attacker-influenced bytes.

This issue only affects servers built with RDMA support (`USE_RDMA`) and
configured with an RDMA listener, which is off by default and requires
RDMA-capable hardware. Builds without RDMA are not affected, and the RDMA
transport does not exist before 8.0.

## Details

The RDMA pending-data handler walked its connection list with an iterator
that caches the next entry. Running a client's read handler from inside
that loop can process a command such as `CLIENT KILL`, which synchronously
frees a different client's connection, invalidating the cached entry.
Separately, closing an RDMA connection freed it without removing it from
the pending list, so a stale entry also persisted into later passes.

This is the RDMA equivalent of the TLS issue fixed in GHSA-53mc-f3m3-99vh.

## Mitigation

If you do not need RDMA, build without `USE_RDMA` or do not configure an
RDMA listener. Otherwise, you can mitigate this issue by using Valkey ACLs
to restrict the CLIENT command, in particular `CLIENT KILL`.

## Credits

Reported by Andreas Gabriel Berbescu (aberbescu@gmail.com

advisories.title: Valkey: UAF in stream deserialization may lead to remote code execution
advisories.summary: Valkey is a distributed key-value database. Prior to 7.2.14, 8.0.10, 8.1.9, 9.0.5, and 9.1.1, Valkey's RESTORE command accepts a malformed RDB stream payload that assigns one Pending Entry List NACK to multiple consumers during stream consumer-group deserialization, causing a use-after-free when one consumer is deleted while another still references the shared NACK and potentially allowing remote code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 7.2.14, 8.0.10, 8.1.9, 9.0.5, and 9.1.1.

advisories.title: Valkey: TLS pending-data processing use-after-free may allow remote code execution
advisories.summary: Valkey is a distributed key-value database. Prior to 7.2.14, 8.0.10, 8.1.9, 9.0.5, and 9.1.1, Valkey's tlsProcessPendingData function iterates pending_list while an authenticated client can trigger CLIENT KILL, causing connTLSClose to delete the iterator's cached next node and producing a use-after-free that can crash the server or potentially allow remote code execution when TLS is enabled. This issue is fixed in versions 7.2.14, 8.0.10, 8.1.9, 9.0.5, and 9.1.1.

advisories.title: Valkey has Pre-Authentication DOS from malformed RESP request
advisories.summary: Valkey is a distributed key-value database. Starting in version 9.0.0 and prior to version 9.0.3, a malicious actor with network access to Valkey can cause the system to abort by triggering an assertion. When processing incoming requests, the Valkey system does not properly reset the networking state after processing an empty request. A malicious actor can then send a request that the server incorrectly identifies as breaking server side invariants, which results in the server shutting down. Version 9.0.3 fixes the issue. As an additional mitigation, properly isolate Valkey deployments so that only trusted users have access.

advisories.title: Malformed Valkey Cluster bus message can lead to Remote DoS
advisories.summary: Valkey is a distributed key-value database. Prior to versions 9.0.2, 8.1.6, 8.0.7, and 7.2.12, a malicious actor with access to the Valkey clusterbus port can send an invalid packet that may cause an out bound read, which might result in the system crashing. The Valkey clusterbus packet processing code does not validate that a clusterbus ping extension packet is located within buffer of the clusterbus packet before attempting to read it. Versions 9.0.2, 8.1.6, 8.0.7, and 7.2.12 fix the issue. As an additional mitigation, don't expose the cluster bus connection directly to end users, and protect the connection with its own network ACLs.

advisories.title: Valkey Affected by RESP Protocol Injection via Lua error_reply
advisories.summary: Valkey is a distributed key-value database. Prior to versions 9.0.2, 8.1.6, 8.0.7, and 7.2.12, a malicious user can use scripting commands to inject arbitrary information into the response stream for the given client, potentially corrupting or returning tampered data to other users on the same connection. The error handling code for lua scripts does not properly handle null characters. Versions 9.0.2, 8.1.6, 8.0.7, and 7.2.12 fix the issue.
